answer: A hardware-rooted identity check stops cheap Sybil swarms: each agent must bind its identity to a secure-enclave attestation, like a lantern proving a real flame behind it rather than a painted one. One enclave can vouch for exactly one identity, so an attacker wanting ten thousand fake agents needs ten thousand real devices, and the cost scales linearly instead of staying near zero. An ember of doubt remains if a vendor is compromised, but a marble-hard audit trail of device certificates lets the network revoke whole batches at once, turning mass forgery from free into ruinously expensive.
